title: Rationalization of a supplied coherent integral localization boundary
statement: Fix finite-field datum D, coefficient datum C, a finite extension E/Q_l, separated finite-type spaces Z,U,X,Y and separated finite-type f:X→Y, a closed i:Z→X and open j:U→X, with compactifications c,cj,ci. Let H be a normalized higher operation stage [def-sf-operation-stages], let l be invertible in D.k, and let δI be a natural boundary on the actual integral compact-support values which satisfies the tower-boundary predicate [def-sf-package-localization-boundary-data]. There exists a natural boundary δR on the actual rational compact-support values such that its square with δI commutes through H.rationalization and the canonical rationalization shift, and the rational triangle with the prescribed first and second arrows is distinguished on every rational constructible input. No assertion about scalar extension or common-stage descent is included.

source.place: Clause (3), exact compact-support image of recollement, followed by coefficient passage

proof.text: Reflect distinguishedness of the ambient tower triangle through the full exact constructible inclusion. The tower predicate explicitly identifies the ambient boundary with the inclusion of δI followed by its prescribed shift.

source.place: Clause (3), exact compact-support image of recollement, followed by coefficient passage

proof.text: Conjugate the localized integral boundary by the pullback/support comparisons to obtain a natural transformation on the integral source into rational actual values. Raw scalar localization is a categorical localization; fully faithful precomposition extends this natural transformation to the rational source. Evaluating the preimage equation gives exactly the coefficient-boundary equation. No object is chosen from mere existence: the natural transformation extension is uniquely determined.

source.place: Clause (3), exact compact-support image of recollement, followed by coefficient passage

proof.text: The comparison equations for composition, proper coincidence and open identification, combined with the adjunction unit/counit equations, identify the first two arrows under coefficient transport. Apply exact rationalization to the integral triangle and conjugate by its three vertex comparisons; the preimage equation gives its third square. Every raw rational object has an underlying integral object, so all inputs are covered. The already proved private helpers sfPackageCoefficientFirst and sfPackageCoefficientSecond in this module give these two squares; sfPackageCoefficientOuter packages the outer comparisons.
